title: Gas Pressure
page_title: Gas Pressure - A Level Chemistry Revision Notes

titles.topic: The Gaseous State: Ideal & Real Gases & pV = nRT

blocks.md: - **Gases **in a container exert a **pressure **as the gas molecules are constantly **colliding **with the wall of the container

blocks.alt: Diagram of a gas showing randomly moving blue particles with arrows in a 3D box, illustrating kinetic molecular theory.
blocks.caption: Gas particles exert a pressure by constantly colliding with the walls of the container

blocks.md:
- **Decreasing **the **volume **(at constant temperature) of the container causes the molecules to be **squashed **together which results in more **frequent** collisions with the container wall
- The **pressure** of the gas **increases**
- The **volume **is therefore **inversely proportional **to the **pressure **(at constant temperature)

  - A graph of the **volume **of gas plotted against 1/pressure gives a straight line

blocks.text: How decreasing the volume of a gas affects collision frequency

blocks.alt: Diagram showing gas molecules in containers. Left: lower pressure, fewer collisions. Right: higher pressure, more collisions. Graph depicts volume vs. inverse pressure line.
blocks.caption: Decreasing the volume of a gas causes an increased collision frequency of the gas particles with the container wall (a); volume is inversely proportional to the pressure (b)

blocks.md:
- **Increasing **the **temperature **(at constant volume) of the gas causes the molecules to gain more **kinetic energy**
- This means that the particles will move **faster** and **collide **with the container walls more **frequently**
- The **pressure **of the gas **increases**
- The **temperature** is therefore **directly proportional **to the **pressure **(at constant volume)

  - A graph of the **temperature **of gas plotted against **pressure **gives a straight line

blocks.text: How increasing the temperature of a gas affects collision frequency

blocks.alt: Diagram depicting gas molecules colliding more frequently with container walls when temperature increases; includes a graph of temperature vs. pressure.
blocks.caption: Increasing the temperature of a gas causes an increased collision frequency of the gas particles with the container wall (a); temperature is directly proportional to the pressure (b)
